chunks: He (Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him) said:
Indeed, God is distinct from His creation, and His creation is distinct from Him; and everything upon which the name 'thing' applies is a creation, apart from God.

key_terms.خَلْق: Creation, creatures — everything that God has brought into being
key_terms.خِلْو: Distinct, separate, free from — denotes absolute ontological separation between Creator and creation
key_terms.شَيْء: Thing — the category of all existents; applying this name to God is rejected as it would make Him a created being
key_terms.مَخْلُوق: Created being — anything bearing the name 'thing' falls into this category

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about God's distinctness from creation?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) articulates the absolute transcendence of God: God is completely distinct from all created things, and all created things are completely distinct from God. The decisive criterion is the use of the word 'thing' (شيء) — anything that can be called a 'thing' is by definition created, whereas God alone transcends this category. This hadith addresses a key theological debate in early Islamic thought about whether it is permissible to apply the word 'thing' to God. The Imam's teaching establishes that God is not a 'thing' among things but exists in an ontological category entirely beyond creation.
